model: Orbital Economy v7.7.16 Cost Pricing candidate r1
note: Task 039, specification §5: 27 new regional/global annotations plus three revised rent annotations; obsolete A Reference Metal Price and A Electronics Reference Price intentionally omitted. Merge into accepted annotations.

Cost Pricing Enabled.role: Switch: cost-based prices enabled in Modes 56–57; 0 by default.
Cost Pricing Enabled.effect: When off, previous 56 modes retain their accepted formulas and values.

Universal Markup.role: Universal cost-price markup: 0.15 for all goods.
Universal Markup.effect: Price = full unit cost × (1 + 0.15), optionally multiplied by scarcity.

Cost Price Signal Time.role: Ten-day smoothing horizon = 10 for price signals.
Cost Price Signal Time.effect: Smoothed stocks break instantaneous circular dependencies of ore, power resources and energy.

A Energy Cost Price Signal.role: Initial energy cost-price signal (A 0.5731; B 0.6787); source prices at time zero with cost pricing enabled.
A Energy Cost Price Signal.effect: Sets starting value of each regional smoothed energy price stock, calibrated to enabled-mode source at t=0.

A Power Resource Cost Price Signal.role: Initial power resource cost-price signal (A 0.31; B 0.4085); source prices at time zero with cost pricing enabled.
A Power Resource Cost Price Signal.effect: Sets starting value of each regional smoothed power resource price stock, calibrated to enabled-mode source at t=0.

A Metal Cost Price Signal.role: Initial metal cost-price signal (A 49.95; B 80.99); source prices at time zero with cost pricing enabled.
A Metal Cost Price Signal.effect: Sets starting value of each regional smoothed metal price stock, calibrated to enabled-mode source at t=0.

A Electronics Cost Price Signal.role: Initial electronics cost-price signal (A 28.32; B 41.12); source prices at time zero with cost pricing enabled.
A Electronics Cost Price Signal.effect: Sets starting value of each regional smoothed electronics price stock, calibrated to enabled-mode source at t=0.

A Capital Goods Cost Price Signal.role: Initial capital goods cost-price signal (A 336.9; B 478.2); source prices at time zero with cost pricing enabled.
A Capital Goods Cost Price Signal.effect: Sets starting value of each regional smoothed capital goods price stock, calibrated to enabled-mode source at t=0.

A Construction Materials Cost Price Sign.role: Initial construction materials cost-price signal (A 109.6; B 148.8); source prices at time zero with cost pricing enabled.
A Construction Materials Cost Price Sign.effect: Sets starting value of each regional smoothed construction materials price stock, calibrated to enabled-mode source at t=0.

A Regolith Cost Price Signal.role: Initial regolith cost-price signal (A 29.69; B 40.15); source prices at time zero with cost pricing enabled.
A Regolith Cost Price Signal.effect: Sets starting value of each regional smoothed regolith price stock, calibrated to enabled-mode source at t=0.

A Reference Metal Price Cost Scale.role: Regional reference metal price calibration scale (A 2.254; B 2.028).
A Reference Metal Price Cost Scale.effect: First-year average price under cost pricing divided by Mode 52 first-year average; stabilises baseline demand and nominal-to-real reference.

A Electronics Reference Price Cost Scale.role: Regional electronics reference price calibration scale (A 1.972; B 2.027).
A Electronics Reference Price Cost Scale.effect: First-year average price under cost pricing divided by Mode 52 first-year average; stabilises baseline demand and nominal-to-real reference.

A Food Index Cost Scale.role: Regional food index reference scale (A 1.754; B 2.475).
A Food Index Cost Scale.effect: Scales the regional food reference in price-index calculation to preserve comparable initial real wages.

A Initial Reference Metal Price.effect: Preserves the accepted numeric reference when cost pricing wraps reference-price formulas; serves as the switch-off branch.

A Initial Electronics Reference Price.effect: Preserves the accepted numeric reference when cost pricing wraps reference-price formulas; serves as the switch-off branch.

A Ore Base Cost.role: Стоимость руды колонии (A 4 / B 14) — главный источник сравнительного преимущества A в металле. With cost pricing enabled, this legacy base amount is economic rent above production unit costs.
A Ore Base Cost.effect: Определяет Ore Price → Metal Unit Cost → Domestic Offer → Market Price. Разрыв ×3.5 делает металл A дешевле (Mode 17 @1080: 30.5 vs 37.4) и задаёт направление торговли металлом A→B на всех сценариях. В v7.4 через Feedstock Price = Market Price это же преимущество переносится на электронику. Under cost_pricing it contributes rent on top of material, energy, labor and depreciation unit costs.
A Ore Base Cost.evidence: Mode 12/17 таблицы (ACCEPTANCE_R2); Mode 4 (Reverse Advantage) меняет именно этот параметр и разворачивает торговлю.; docs/research/COST_PRICES_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-16_RU.md; docs/tasks/039-cost-pricing/V7_7_16_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md §5; ARCHIVE/evidence/042-cost-pricing-node/calibrate.mjs.

A Power Generation Cost.role: Себестоимость генерации (A 0.08 / B 0.03 за единицу энергии). With cost pricing enabled, this legacy base amount is economic rent above production unit costs.
A Power Generation Cost.effect: Базовая цена энергии до дефицитной надбавки; B энергетически дешевле, но энергия не торгуется, поэтому это влияет только на локальные unit cost (Energy per Metal 30 → 2.4 vs 0.9 на единицу металла). Under cost_pricing it contributes rent on top of material, energy, labor and depreciation unit costs.
A Power Generation Cost.evidence: Mode 10 (Cheap Energy) тестирует именно этот канал.; docs/research/COST_PRICES_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-16_RU.md; docs/tasks/039-cost-pricing/V7_7_16_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md §5; ARCHIVE/evidence/042-cost-pricing-node/calibrate.mjs.

Base Power Resource Price.role: Base physical operating-resource price. With cost pricing enabled, this legacy base amount is economic rent above production unit costs.
Base Power Resource Price.effect: Adds an explicit resource-cost component to generation when Energy Kernel v2 is enabled. Under cost_pricing it contributes rent on top of material, energy, labor and depreciation unit costs.
